facts.claim: This study was published in Frontiers in Psychology, Volume 17, on 25 May 2026, with DOI 10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1794353; authors are Xiaojun Ling, Mengqi Li, and Jiahui Sun.
facts.subject: Article publication metadata

facts.claim: The study investigates whether screen time mediates the association between close vs conflictual parent-child relationships and behavioral problems (externalizing and internalizing) in children aged 3 to 6, using a longitudinal design with three waves 4 months apart.
facts.subject: Study aim

facts.claim: The final analytic sample included 532 children (289 boys, 54.3%; 243 girls, 45.7%) with a mean age of 3.99 years (SD=0.85); initial recruitment was 619 at T1, 588 at T2, and 532 at T3; attrition of 87 participants (14.1%) occurred, with no significant differences between retained and dropped participants.
facts.subject: Study sample and attrition
facts.date_or_period: Not specified; three waves spaced 4 months apart
facts.conditions: Children aged 3 to 6 from Fuyang City, Anhui Province, China
facts.numeric_value: n=532 final; 619 T1; 588 T2; mean age 3.99 (SD=0.85); attrition 87 (14.1%)

facts.claim: Data were collected from mothers at three time points (T1 n=619, T2 n=588, T3 n=532), each spaced 4 months apart; all questionnaires were completed by mothers.
facts.subject: Data collection design
facts.numeric_value: 3 waves spaced 4 months apart; T1 n=619, T2 n=588, T3 n=532

facts.claim: Parent-child relationship was measured using the Child-Parent Relationship Scale (CPRS), Chinese revised version, with Closeness (7 items) and Conflict (8 items) subscales rated on a 5-point Likert scale; internal consistency was Cronbach's α=0.882 for Closeness and 0.895 for Conflict.
facts.subject: Measurement of parent-child relationship

facts.claim: Screen time was assessed via caregiver reports on two items: average daily electronic device use on weekdays and weekends, weighted as (weekday average x 5 + weekend average x 2)/7.
facts.subject: Measurement of screen time
facts.notes_for_writer: Does not capture content or context of screen use.

facts.claim: Behavioral problems were measured using the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ); externalizing problems comprised Hyperactivity/Inattention and Conduct Problems, internalizing problems comprised Emotional Symptoms and Peer Problems; reliability was Cronbach's α=0.891 for externalizing and 0.853 for internalizing.
facts.subject: Measurement of behavioral problems

facts.claim: Screen time was negatively correlated with close parent-child relationship (r=-0.077, p<0.001) and positively correlated with conflictual parent-child relationship (r=0.206, p<0.001); it also correlated positively with peer problems (r=0.077, p<0.05), emotional symptoms (r=0.161, p<0.001), conduct problems (r=0.106, p<0.01), and hyperactivity/inattention (r=0.143, p<0.001).
facts.subject: Bivariate correlations with screen time
facts.numeric_value: r=-0.077 (closeness), r=0.206 (conflict), r=0.077 (peer problems), r=0.161 (emotional symptoms), r=0.106 (conduct problems), r=0.143 (hyperactivity/inattention)
facts.ambiguity: Time points for correlations not explicitly stated in text.

facts.claim: Conflictual parent-child relationship significantly predicted higher screen time (β=0.208, p<0.001, 95% CI [0.094, 0.322]).
facts.subject: Conflictual parent-child relationship predicting screen time
facts.date_or_period: T1 relationship to T2 screen time

facts.claim: Close parent-child relationship did not significantly predict screen time (β=0.006, p>0.05, 95% CI [-0.088, 0.100]).
facts.subject: Close parent-child relationship predicting screen time
facts.date_or_period: T1 relationship to T2 screen time

facts.claim: Screen time at T2 significantly predicted internalizing (β=0.148, p<0.05, 95% CI [0.011, 0.285]) and externalizing (β=0.149, p<0.05, 95% CI [0.016, 0.282]) behavioral problems at T3.
facts.subject: Screen time predicting behavioral problems
facts.date_or_period: T2 screen time to T3 behavioral problems
facts.numeric_value: IBP β=0.148, p<0.05; EBP β=0.149, p<0.05; CIs as listed
facts.ambiguity: Narrative text reports p<0.001 for these paths, while Table 3 lists p<0.05.

facts.claim: Conflictual parent-child relationship directly predicted higher internalizing (β=0.476, p<0.001, 95% CI [0.302, 0.650]) and externalizing (β=0.273, p<0.05, 95% CI [0.118, 0.428]) behavioral problems.
facts.subject: Conflictual parent-child relationship predicting behavioral problems
facts.date_or_period: T1 relationship to T3 behavioral problems
facts.numeric_value: IBP β=0.476, p<0.001; EBP β=0.273, p<0.05; CIs as listed
facts.ambiguity: Discrepancy for externalizing p-value between text (p<0.001) and Table (p<0.05).

facts.claim: Close parent-child relationship directly predicted lower internalizing (β=-0.157, p<0.001, 95% CI [-0.294, -0.020]) and externalizing (β=-0.213, p<0.001, 95% CI [-0.346, -0.080]) behavioral problems.
facts.subject: Close parent-child relationship predicting behavioral problems
facts.date_or_period: T1 relationship to T3 behavioral problems
facts.numeric_value: IBP β=-0.157; EBP β=-0.213; CIs as listed

facts.claim: Screen time partially mediated the effect of conflictual parent-child relationship on internalizing (indirect β=0.031, p<0.05, 95% CI [-0.026, 0.088]) and externalizing (indirect β=0.031, p<0.05, 95% CI [-0.022, 0.084]) behavioral problems; no significant mediation was found for close parent-child relationship (indirect β=-0.001, p>0.05 for both outcomes).
facts.subject: Mediation by screen time
facts.date_or_period: T1 relationship to T2 screen time to T3 behavioral problems
facts.numeric_value: Conflict indirect β=0.031; closeness indirect β=-0.001; CIs include zero
facts.causal_strength: Partial mediation; causal interpretation not definitive
facts.ambiguity: Confidence intervals for the indirect effects include zero, inconsistent with reported p<0.05.

facts.claim: The partial mediation model showed acceptable fit: χ²(7)=19.27, p<0.05; RMSEA=0.057, 90% CI [0.028, 0.089]; CFI=0.950; TLI=0.917; SRMR=0.028; partial mediation fit significantly better than full mediation (Δχ²(2)=15.30, p<0.001).
facts.subject: Model fit of partial mediation model

facts.claim: Family SES significantly affected internalizing (F=3.741, p<0.05) and externalizing (F=3.198, p<0.05) behavioral problems; low-SES children scored higher than high-SES children on both, with no significant differences between middle and high SES or middle and low SES.
facts.subject: Family SES and behavioral problems

facts.claim: The study did not include baseline levels of key variables, so indirect effects may partially reflect pre-existing differences rather than developmental processes; caution is warranted when interpreting causal implications.
facts.subject: Study limitation (no autoregressive control)

facts.claim: The short-term longitudinal design (four-month intervals) and single-informant maternal reports limit generalizability and causal inference; screen time was measured only as duration, not content/context, and the nested data structure was not modeled.
facts.subject: Generalizability and design limitations

facts.claim: The study concludes that conflictual parent-child relationships predict later internalizing and externalizing problems partially mediated by screen time; relational closeness directly predicts fewer externalizing behaviors and is not associated with screen time.
facts.subject: Conclusions on parent-child relationship, screen time, and behavioral problems
